I. Introduction The Synthesis of COnsists as Rolling Energy microgrids (SCORE**) toolset assesses the impact of new energy technologies on railroad performance, with current and future combinations of technologies including Diesel, Hydrogen, and different battery technologies. Its intended users include researchers, government and industry. Its goals are to interactively and in real-time, create trade spaces to explore the impact of different powering technologies have on fuel costs and Green House Gas (GHG) emissions when used to power while varying the number and type of freights cars, while traversing different routes, and while changing different operating characteristics for powering the consist such as reduced maximum speed and powering policy optimization. To achieve these goals, an easy-to-use, web-based application is made publically available. It can simulate individual consists traveling a given route in about 5 seconds or less, generate an optimal powering policy in about 15 seconds and generating meaningful trade spaces within a few minutes. At the heart of the SCORE toolset is an Energy-Longitudinal Train Dynamics (E-LTD) model that treats the train as a single degree of freedom spread mass system moving over a route with speed restrictions, curves, and elevation changes, and that calculates the energy flows required to move a consist along a route following a powering policy. In the E-LTD, energy flows from stored sources such as diesel fuel, batteries, and hydrogen. This stored energy is converted to mechanical power with levels of efficiency and maximum rates given by the chosen technologies. This power passes through transmissions to eventually apply force to track with the locomotive drive wheels. The energy stored in diesel and hydrogen can only be consumed. The energy stored in the batteries can be either consumed or regenerated through dynamic braking, with the source of energy for regeneration being elevation changes, decelerations, or consuming excess power from other locomotive power sources (transferring power through the rail). * Assistant Professor Industrial Engineering † Associate Professor Aerospace Engineering ‡ Research Engineer § Research Engineer ** https://www.scorelocomotives.org/ 2 The SCORE toolset includes four primary elements: 1) route generate, 2) consist generation, 3) energy-LTD, and 4) trade space exploration (see Fig. 1). SCORE allows users to select routes based upon the destination and origin, both configure and select consists to travel over the selected route, configure new locomotives, and select a powering policy to specify the sources of power used by the consist as it traverses the route. A given route specifies distances, gradients, curvatures, and maximum speeds along the route. A consist is made up of an ordered list of locomotives and trailing stock. A locomotive is defined by its energy source and capacity, conversion efficiencies, and maximum power.
